title: Is the sum of two such even numbers a multiple of four?
description: Twelve plus sixteen and twenty two plus six are written in the forms four p plus four q and four p plus two plus four q plus two, and each sum is shown to be a multiple of four. The two leftovers of two make one more full row. Keeko raises the doubt that twenty two plus six cannot be a multiple of four because neither number is.
teaching_notes: One idea: two leftovers of two dots together make four dots, which is one more full row of four. Watch for students who think a sum of two numbers that are not multiples of four cannot be a multiple of four.

source: Show that 12 + 16 and 22 + 6 are multiples of 4, using the f
video_script.why: A learner writes two even numbers in the forms four p and four p plus two, adds them, and sees why the sum is a multiple of four.
video_script.substitution: the book's own sums: twelve plus sixteen, and twenty two plus six
video_script.anchor: dots in rows of four, with the dots left over set apart, as in the book
video_script.wrong_answer: twenty two plus six cannot be a multiple of four because neither is
video_script.wrong_move: thinks a sum cannot be a multiple of four when neither number is, forgetting the two leftovers join
video_script.payoff_line: Twelve plus sixteen and twenty two plus six both make twenty eight, a multiple of four.

final_answer.value: 12 + 16 and 22 + 6 both make 28, a multiple of 4
final_answer.spoken: twelve plus sixteen and twenty two plus six both make twenty eight, a multiple of four

hold_back: 12 + 16 and 22 + 6 both make 28, a multiple of 4
video_script.design: One idea: two leftovers of two make one more full row of four. Assumes the forms four p and four p plus two. Wrong idea: neither number is a multiple of four, so the sum is not. Dots in rows of four stay on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about adding even numbers and rows of four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The sums are twelve plus sixteen, and twenty two plus six. Are both of them multiples of four?

beats.on_screen: the two sum cards stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a number of the form 4p as full rows of four; a number of the form 4p + 2 as full rows with two dots apart; two sets of two dots join into one more row

marks.full: a number of the form four p is shown as full rows of four
marks.two: a number of the form four p plus two has two dots set apart
marks.join: two sets of two dots join into one more row of four

narration: <bookmark mark='full'/>A number of the form four p fills full rows of four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>A number of the form four p plus two has two dots left over.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Two sets of two left over dots make four dots, which is one more full row.

marks.given: the two sums and the two forms are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the sums are twelve plus sixteen and twenty two plus six, with two forms to use.

beats.on_screen: To find: show that both sums are multiples of 4
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to show that both sums are multiples of four.

marks.forms: twelve and sixteen are written as four times three and four times four
marks.sum: the rows join: four times the bracket three plus four, then four times seven, then twenty eight

narration: <bookmark mark='forms'/>Step one, use the form four p plus four q. Twelve is four times three, and sixteen is four times four.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The sum is four times the bracket three plus four, which is four times seven, or twenty eight.

marks.twentytwo: twenty two is five full rows and two dots apart
marks.six: six is one full row and two dots apart

narration: <bookmark mark='twentytwo'/>Step two, use the form four p plus two for the next sum. Twenty two is four times five, plus two.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Six is four times one, plus two.

marks.left: the two leftovers of two sit together as four dots
marks.row: the four dots become one more full row
marks.total: the rows total seven, so twenty eight

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, add them. The two leftovers of two make four.
<bookmark mark='row'/>Four is one more full row, so the rows are five, then one, then one more.
<bookmark mark='total'/>That is four times the bracket five plus one plus one. It is four times seven, or twenty eight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 12 + 16 and 22 + 6 both make 28, a multiple of 4
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Twelve plus sixteen and twenty two plus six both make twenty eight, a multiple of four.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the dot rows
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 22 and 6 each with a gap at the end of the last row, a cross over their sum, struck through; the two gaps join and fill a row

marks.doubt: the bubble with twenty two and six, each with a gap, appears
marks.gaps: the two gaps of two dots glow
marks.fix: the gaps join into a full row and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks twenty two plus six cannot be a multiple of four because neither is.
<bookmark mark='gaps'/>But look at the leftovers. Each number leaves two dots over.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Two leftovers together fill a row, so the sum is a multiple of four.
